findings.fact: The local root is checked only as an existing non-symlink directory covered by a fresh-source/suffix hf3fs mount. validate_manifest separately validates the writer root and round directories. No check binds the local checker root relative to its mount target to the writer root relative to the writer mount target before check_deleted_paths.
findings.static_counterexample: A valid writer manifest records A mount/test with its six exact run-bound sample names. Supply B mount/other as an existing empty directory on the otherwise exact fresh hf3fs mount. Both identity validations pass, but the 600 lstat calls check unrelated mount/other/sample/file paths, all absent, producing DATA_RECORDED without checking the actual writer namespace.
findings.impact: 600 actual ENOENT alone can falsely qualify namespace visibility. Do not run/use this checker as qualified baseline absence evidence.
findings.minimal_fix: Before any lstat, require exact matching plain mount-relative writer/checker root, or restrict both to one fixed namespace-relative root. Record the mapped root in the receipt. Add a guard for a safe existing wrong root on an otherwise valid fresh mount and require rejection before lstat.
findings.related_path_guard: Reject literal .. components and avoid symlink/lexical-only root mapping bypasses while implementing this same root binding; no new workload/fault matrix is required.

positive_findings: Fixed upstream commit, existing ARM64 patch and Owner primitive SHA are recorded and helper SHA/shape are checked before writer operation. The tool says reference-only DATA_RECORDED and UNOBSERVED cache, not stock, paired candidate, strong-data qualification or formal G2.25 PASS.
Writer reuses Owner prepare/full-content verification/timed_unlink primitives; all preparation and directory synchronization/cleanup remain outside the helper unlink timer.

Manifest validates writer role, upstream/patch/helper identities, digits-digits run ID, shape, all six rounds, exact run/round sample names and directory strings, expected file list and preparation/content/timer/cleanup outcome fields.
Check_deleted_paths performs real lstat per path and rejects PRESENT, non-ENOENT and permission errors. This remains insufficient until the checker-root mapping blocker is fixed.

Ordinary sample exceptions return a failed sample, leave residual paths as evidence, persist each returned sample immediately and break on failure. Fresh output mkdir prevents overwriting historical output; existing output sentinel guard is meaningful.

saved_Linux_guards.scope: Read saved r2 raw only, did not execute
saved_Linux_guards.limits: The six passed guards do not cover wrong existing checker root mapping. Existing tests call check_deleted_paths on a temporary unrelated root directly, so they cannot establish complete checker admission correctness.

limitations: Static review only; no Linux/product/FS test or services run by reviewer.
No fixture review, new 3FS execution, strong durability investigation or broad POSIX expansion in this report.
Writer timing logic is not invalidated by the checker-root binding finding. No baseline workload has been qualified by this tool review.
preservation: Retain this original FAIL and its exact two source identities. A repaired driver/test pair requires a separate review artifact and affected Linux guard evidence; do not overwrite this finding.
